feature: hexa grades JavaScript as it grades TypeScript

exempt.reason: §8 says what the decision does not cover (a JavaScript scaffold and the type-based checks); it makes no behaviour to test

specs.description: A JavaScript file in domain/ that imports an adapter is a boundary violation in the grade.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js contains an ES import of ../adapters/secondary/http.js; src/adapters/secondary/http.js exists
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: The report names a boundary violation from src/domain/order.js to src/adapters/secondary/http.js, the violation count in the grade includes it, and src/domain/order.js counts in the graded and in-a-layer files.

specs.description: A .mjs and a .cjs file are graded source.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/a.mjs and src/domain/b.cjs each import ../adapters/secondary/http.js (src/adapters/secondary/http.js exists)
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: Both src/domain/a.mjs and src/domain/b.cjs are reported as boundary violations and are counted among the files in a layer.

specs.description: A JavaScript file under node_modules, or one removed by analyze.exclude, is not graded.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; node_modules/pkg/x.js and src/domain/legacy.js each import an adapter; .hexa/project.json lists src/domain/legacy.js in analyze.exclude
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: Neither file is reported as a violation or counted as a graded file; the excluded file is counted as excluded, as for every language.

specs.description: A CommonJS require with a string literal is an import edge.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js contains const h = require('../adapters/secondary/http.js'); src/adapters/secondary/http.js exists
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: There is an import edge from src/domain/order.js to src/adapters/secondary/http.js and it is reported as a boundary violation.

specs.description: A require whose argument is not a string literal makes no edge and is not guessed.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js contains const h = require(name) and const k = require('./' + dir + '/x')
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: No import edge is created from those calls, no violation is reported for them, and hexa does not fail.

specs.description: A relative specifier without an extension resolves across the six extensions and to a folder's index.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js imports ./item and ./pricing; src/domain/item.mjs and src/domain/pricing/index.cjs exist
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: There are import edges from src/domain/order.js to src/domain/item.mjs and to src/domain/pricing/index.cjs, and neither is reported as unresolved.

specs.description: A .js specifier resolves to the .ts file the compiler would map it to when that file exists, else to the .js file.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/a.ts imports ./b.js and ./c.js; src/usecases/b.ts exists and src/usecases/c.js exists
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: The edge for ./b.js goes to src/usecases/b.ts and the edge for ./c.js goes to src/usecases/c.js.

specs.description: A specifier that names no project file is unchanged, and stays external.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js contains require('lodash') and import x from 'left-pad'; there is no project file of those names
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: No import edge to a project file is created and no violation is reported for them.

specs.description: A jsconfig.json paths map is read as a tsconfig.json one is.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; jsconfig.json has compilerOptions.paths {'@/*': ['./src/*']}; src/domain/order.js imports '@/adapters/secondary/http' and src/adapters/secondary/http.js exists
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: The import resolves to src/adapters/secondary/http.js and is reported as a boundary violation.

specs.description: A paths alias that matches a pattern but names no project file is left as written.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; jsconfig.json maps '@/*' to ./src/*; src/domain/order.js imports '@/missing/thing'; no such file exists
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: No edge to a project file is created and no violation is reported for that import.

specs.description: module.exports and exports.x define the module's exports for dead-export detection.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/util.js contains module.exports = { used, unused } and exports.extra = 1; src/usecases/app.js requires ./util and reads only .used
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: unused and extra are reported as dead exports of src/usecases/util.js and used is not.

specs.description: An export another file imports is not dead, in any spelling.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/util.js has module.exports = { a } and export const b = 1; src/usecases/app.js does const { a } = require('./util') and src/usecases/main.js does import { b } from './util.js'
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: Neither a nor b is reported as a dead export.

specs.description: Test files in the four extensions and under __tests__ are test files, and entry points are not dead.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/x.test.js, src/usecases/y.spec.mjs and src/usecases/__tests__/z.cjs exist; src/usecases/index.js exports a name nothing imports
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: The three files are treated as test files, not as source with dead exports, and the export of src/usecases/index.js is not reported as dead.

specs.description: A file whose name merely contains test is not a test file, and an ordinary file's unused export is dead.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/latest.js and src/usecases/contest.js exist; src/usecases/helper.js exports a name nothing imports
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: latest.js and contest.js are graded as source, and the unused export of helper.js is reported as dead.

specs.description: An fs or node: import or require in domain/ is a policy violation under the shipped deny list.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; the shipped .hexa/ADR-rules.toml import policy; src/domain/order.js contains require('fs') and import cp from 'node:child_process'
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: Both are reported as import-policy violations of the domain.

specs.description: The same fs import in an adapter is allowed.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; the shipped .hexa/ADR-rules.toml import policy; src/adapters/secondary/store.js contains require('fs')
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: No import-policy violation is reported for it.

specs.description: @hexa:public keeps a JavaScript export out of the dead-export check.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/api.js has a line comment @hexa:public above exports.entry = run, and nothing imports entry
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: entry is not reported as a dead export.

specs.description: Without the tag the same export is dead.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/usecases/api.js has exports.entry = run with no tag and nothing imports entry
specs.when: hexa analyze runs on the project
specs.then: entry is reported as a dead export.

specs.description: hexa analyze --file checks one JavaScript file.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/order.js imports ../adapters/secondary/http.js (which exists)
specs.when: hexa analyze . --file src/domain/order.js runs
specs.then: It reports the boundary violation for that file and exits 1.

specs.description: A clean JavaScript file passes --file, and a JavaScript file is never reported clean without being read.
specs.given: A TypeScript-style project (package.json) with src/domain/, src/adapters/secondary/ and src/usecases/; src/domain/clean.js imports only ./item.js (src/domain/item.js exists); hexa analyze . --file src/domain/clean.js runs; and in the same project a JavaScript file in analyze.exclude is also present
specs.when: hexa analyze . and hexa analyze . --file src/domain/clean.js run
specs.then: --file exits 0 for the clean file; hexa analyze . counts the excluded JavaScript file as excluded, not as graded and not as clean.
